newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to draw down on $130 mln IMF loan in July.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to draw down on $130 mln IMF loan in July.

text.p: Bulgaria will draw down by end of July on a more than $130 million International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan to balance payments made to foreign creditors, the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) governor said on Monday.
"Bulgaria will draw down on the (IMF standby loan) second tranche by the end of this month to balance payments to foreign lenders," Svetoslav Gavriiski told reporters.
On Friday Bulgaria's Finance Ministry ordered more than $130 million in Brady bond coupons to be transferred by the BNB to the debt agent Citibank of Citicorp to distribute payments to investors.
Payments were also made to the IMF this month, a BNB official said, declining to specify the amount.
The IMF on Wednesday approved the release of a more than $130 million second tranche, following the first review of a 14-month $510 standby agreement approved in April.
After the tranche is drawn down it becomes a BNB Banking Department liability, which should be balanced by an increase of government debt managed by the department.
"Bulgaria expects to receive the next IMF tranche of $84.5 million by mid-August without another review of the country's structural reform performance," Gavriiski said.

The $31.7 million first tranche of the standby was disbursed in mid-April along with $147 million under the cereal element of the Compensatory and Contingency Financing Facility to fund increased grain import costs. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
